meta.title: Pandora
meta.author: skyrunner (Brain Control)
meta.description: The soundtrack of Pandora by Brain Control (April 2011). Brain Control's 64K intro that won the PC 64K intro competition at Revision 2011. Music by skyrunner (credited in the intro's readme and pouet), made with Tunefish 3, the synthesizer of Brain Control's Enigma Studio 3. 125 BPM, 4:07, 21 tracks, 3003 note cells. This is an adapted version, not the original recording: the song and its instruments were read from the released executable (tools/tf3-extract: the kkrunchy stub emulated until the intro starts, then the synth block found in the unpacked image; parameters stored in the 2011 engine's older layout, as percentages), converted by `synth-convert e3prj` in player mode with the 2011 engine's laws (`--engine 2011`) to the unified synth (points and PAD table oscillators, Tunefish 3 decimation stage, insert effects as track devices) and imported with `song import` (notes rounded to 960 ticks per beat). No reference renderer exists for that engine: against a capture of the released intro it differs by at most 3.89 dB in any octave band from 63 Hz to 8 kHz. The 2011 engine clips each unison layer on its own and adds an offset before its oscillator drive; the unified synth does neither, so the layered instruments sound quieter than in the intro. The random per-note detune (slop) is not converted. Track names are derived here from each track's notes; the executable does not store the authors' names. No licence is stated: the music belongs to its authors. It is published here as an adapted reference copy while Brain Control is asked for permission, and is removed at the authors' request.
